title: Add CI dependency graph sanitizer and lint-cost estimator
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a CI-side dependency graph sanitizer and a presubmit lint cost estimator. Non-breaking. Improves presubmit latency and reduces noise from transient deps.
body:
Context and motivation: Over the past quarter we've seen CI presubmit latency regressions largely driven by two factors: long-running lint shards run on PRs that touch large scope, and false-positive failures triggered by stale transitive dependencies during deterministic dependency resolution. This PR introduces two coordinated features to reduce noise and improve feedback speed: 1) a CI Dependency Graph Sanitizer that runs in a presubmit gate and emits a compact sanitized-graph.json artifact when it detects stale/transitive anomalies; 2) a lightweight Lint Cost Estimator that computes an estimated lint-time score for a PR and short-circuits full lint shards when the estimate is below a safety threshold while still running fast linters and staged checks.

Summary of changes (single-line commits): commit 1: add ci/tooling/dep-sanitzer entrypoint and graph-normalizer; commit 2: add ci/tooling/lint-cost-estimator; commit 3: wire sanitizer into workflow .github/workflows/presubmit-deps.yml; commit 4: integrate estimator into staged-lint runner and update docs; commit 5: add unit tests + small e2e smoke script for workspace sampling.

Checklist: - [x] design doc linked ENG-4312 - [x] unit tests for graph normalizer - [x] integration tests for estimator fallback behavior - [x] small benchmark showing reduced lint runtime - [x] docs updated for dev onboarding

Files changed (high-level): - ci/tooling/dep_sanitizer.py (graph normalization, provenances) - ci/tooling/lint_cost.py (estimator heuristics & cache) - .github/workflows/presubmit-deps.yml (adds sanitizer job + artifact) - .github/workflows/staged-lint.yml (estimator fastpath hook) - docs/dev/ci.md (new section: presubmit fastpath & dep sanitization) - tests/ci/test_dep_sanitize.py - tests/ci/test_lint_cost.py

Small illustrative snippet (sanitizer summary JSON emitted as artifact): {"sanitized_nodes": 312, "removed_transitive": 14, "heuristic_note": "trimmed optional-node paths that resolve to duplicate hashes"}

Why this approach: The sanitizer is intentionally conservative: it never mutates build manifests; it only emits a sanitized graph and an advisory summary. CI policies can be configured to fail only on 'determinism' regressions (hash mismatches) not heuristic trims. The lint estimator uses a historical sample of lint shard runtimes driven by path-level fingerprints and a cached relic (sha -> percentile). On small diffs the estimator will allow a 'fastpath' that runs a curated, much lighter lint set (formatting, banned patterns, critical linters) while queuing full lint in an async job if the owner requests it.

Benchmarks (presubmit on redwood monorepo): - baseline median presubmit-lint wall-clock: 13m42s - with estimator fastpath applied to 60% of small PRs: median presubmit-lint wall-clock: 4m10s - sanitizer detected 28 presubmit-time transitive anomalies in trial window; triage reduced 4 flakey failures to advisory-only.

Review conversation (high level): - Marco Ruiz (reviewer): "This looks promising; can we ensure the estimator doesn't hide security-related linters?" - Author (Aisha): "Yes — estimator always includes security-critical checks; added a test fixture verifying that rule." - Elena Kim: "Consider exposing a toggle in console for teams to opt into strict sanitizer enforcement." - Author: "Good idea; added a small config block (ci.team_config.sanitizer.mode) and documented default 'advisory' mode." - Jonas Berg (approval): "LGTM after addressing flaky RNG seed in tests." - CI bot: initial presubmit fails on test/test_lint_cost intermittently; rerun passed.

CI summary and notable failures: - Unit tests: passed (local 8/8) - Integration: flaky on first run due to non-deterministic test in test_lint_cost.py (fixed: seed set) - Presubmit workflow: sanitizer job runs in ~12s for graph extraction, normalization added ~6s overhead to presubmit but prevented downstream 5–10min debug cycles.

Operational notes and migration: - Default behavior is opt-in via .github/ci_teams.yaml; repo-level default remains advisory. - Ops: added a lightweight monitor in console for 'sanitizer advisories' under CI -> Presubmit Issues. - Rollout plan: staged rollout to teams: infra (week 0), sdk (week 1), core redwood (week 2). - Backout plan: remove workflow hook or set ci.team_config.sanitizer.mode = "off".

Security and compliance: no new secrets; sanitizer runs with existing read-only dependency graph access. Estimator uses cached historical metrics stored in CI artifact store with read access limited to ci-agent service account.

Merge outcome: squash-merged into main on 2025-02-20 by Marco Ruiz. Follow-ups: ENG-4399 (add console toggles) and ENG-4421 (extend estimator to rust & go codepaths).

Contact: author Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai) for follow-up and rollout coordination.
